analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata. ProviderLoopConfig.swift:40-43,67,85 adds a default-off member update-drain flag without changing model eligibility or authorization. ClusterServiceAgent.swift:79-87 adds two fixed paths, not file access or execution. ClusterMemberUpdateSlot.swift:17-20 changes documentation only; scheduling remains unchanged. The supplied ProviderLoop.swift:1023-1294 excerpt has no changed lines; orientation identifies new drain ownership/task state at 566-569, whose use is outside this batch.
ClusterPairUpdate.swift:13-26 introduces bounded coordination/drain timing; :53-78 gates progress by target, phase and working-progress freshness; :81-119 introduces age-limited local restart requests and delegated file I/O. No independently supported security regression follows from these helpers alone. No visible changes affect encryption, prompt/cache exposure (A-001/T-041), credential custody, billing or serving grants (A-016/T-053/T-054).
Integration must examine ClusterPairUpdateCycle, ProviderLoop+ClusterUpdateDrain, configuration call sites, progress transport and ClusterSupervisionFiles. Material contracts remain unverified: adversarial partner progress must not substitute for artifact verification or current pair approval; the running==target shortcut at ClusterPairUpdate.swift:57 and timestamp/phase readiness must not allow stale progress to stop active work. Verify actual admission closure, cancellation/reopening and drain ownership across coordinator and local HTTP requests (A-018/T-010/T-043), plus bounded, owner-checked control-file reads/writes and request consumption. These controls are outside supplied evidence, not observed omissions.
